newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean futures end mixed in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean futures end mixed in dull trade.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mixed in dull trading on Tuesday on a lack of fresh market-moving news, traders said.
The most actively traded November 1997 contract ended at 3,162 yuan ($381) per tonne, unchanged from Monday's close. It opened at an intraday low of 3,160 and a high of 3,170 yuan.
September fell four to 3,154, the January 1998 contract rose 30 to 3,148 and March fell 100 to 3,055 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume rose to 27,900 tonnes from 19,200 tonnes.
Soybeans opened mixed and moved around the opening level for most of the session, traders said.
"A lack of market-moving news made trading very dull today, with only speculators pushing up the prices up and down," said one trader.
"But the technical charts show that soybean futures have downward potential," he said.
Traders said they expected soybeans to meet strong resistance at high levels in the next few days but that sharp falls were also unlikely with no new stimulus around the corner.
